title: Check: admission control
description: Five questions on the last gate before persistence.

questions.prompt: Where does admission sit in the request pipeline?

options.text: After authorisation, before validation and persistence

questions.explanation: Authenticate, authorise, admit, validate, persist. Admission is the last chance to change or refuse an object.

questions.prompt: Which runs first, mutating or validating webhooks?
questions.explanation: Mutating first so that validation sees the final object - otherwise a defaulting webhook could smuggle something past a check.

questions.prompt: A webhook is unreachable and its failurePolicy is Fail. What happens?
questions.explanation: Which is safe but can wedge a cluster if the webhook's own Pods cannot start. Scope it with namespaceSelector.

questions.prompt: Which built-in admission plugin stops a kubelet from modifying other nodes' objects?
questions.explanation: NodeRestriction is why --authorization-mode=Node,RBAC is the standard pairing.

questions.prompt: How is Pod Security enforced today?

options.text: With the Pod Security admission controller, configured by namespace labels

questions.explanation: PodSecurityPolicy was removed. Labels like pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted are the replacement.
